criteria.title: Requirements
items: A dependent must meet the support, income and property requirements (National Health Insurance Act Enforcement Rule Art. 2).

Support: a spouse always qualifies. Parents, grandparents and children qualify when living together; living apart adds conditions by relationship. A child's spouse and a spouse's child qualify only when living together (Annex 1).

Income: total income must be ₩20 million a year or less. There must be no business income, but up to ₩5 million counts as none if there is no business registration or they have a disability grade. Housing rental income removes the no-registration exemption (Annex 1-2).

Property: a total property tax base of ₩540 million or less is fine. Between ₩540 million and ₩900 million, total income must be ₩10 million or less; above ₩900 million never qualifies. Siblings must be at or below ₩180 million (Annex 1-2).
Siblings qualify only if under 30, 65 or older, registered disabled, or merit/veteran recipients with a disability grade, and never married (divorced or widowed counts).
If the person is married, both spouses must meet the income requirement.

income.title: How income is counted
items: Interest, dividends, business, employment, pension and other income are added up; tax-free income is excluded (Enforcement Decree Art. 41(1)).
Public pensions (National, civil service, teachers', military) count in full (Decree Art. 41(1)5).
Employment income is gross pay minus tax-free items; business and other income are revenue minus necessary expenses (Enforcement Rule Art. 44(1)).

Financial income: premium calculations skip interest and dividends totalling ₩10 million or less (Rule Art. 44(1) proviso). It is not confirmed whether the dependent test does the same, so this calculator includes it and flags when excluding it would change the result.
Whether private pensions (pension savings, IRP) count is not covered here. Please check with the NHIS.

timing.title: When it applies
items: In November and December, the review uses the previous year's income. For example, November 2026 uses 2025 income (Decree Art. 41(3)).
From January to October, it uses income from two years before, except pensions, which use the previous year.
Property uses that year's June 1 property tax data from November to the following October (NHIS Articles of Association Art. 43-4).
If the requirements are not met, dependent status ends the day after the NHIS confirms it (Rule Art. 2(3)).
If the dependent is reported within 90 days of the employee member's enrolment or change date, it is recognised from that date (Rule Art. 2(2)).

reform.title: What changed in September 2022
items: The second-stage premium reform (effective Sept 1, 2022) lowered the income limit for dependents from ₩34 million to ₩20 million a year.
The plan to tighten the property limit to ₩360 million was dropped; the ₩540 million limit (₩540–900 million with income of ₩10 million or less) stayed.
About 273,000 dependents (1.5%) were expected to become regional members; their temporary premium reduction (80% in year one down to 20% in year four) ran until August 2026.

tips.title: Worth checking
items: If pensions, interest and other income are close to ₩20 million, add them up before the November review.
Above a ₩540 million property tax base, the income limit drops to ₩10 million. Look at property and income together.
With a business registration, even a little business income fails the business income requirement.
The NHIS website's dependent eligibility check (simulation) shows the result based on NHIS data.

items.q: What is the income limit for a dependent?
items.a: Interest, dividends, business, employment, pension and other income together must be ₩20 million a year or less. There should be no business income, but up to ₩5 million counts as none without a business registration. Housing rental income removes that exemption, while registered disabled people and merit/veteran recipients with a disability grade get the ₩5 million allowance regardless of registration (Enforcement Rule Annex 1-2).

items.q: Can someone lose dependent status with only a National Pension?
items.a: Yes. Public pensions such as the National Pension count in full as income (Enforcement Decree Art. 41(1)5). If total income exceeds ₩20 million a year (about ₩1.66 million a month), the income requirement fails. Above a ₩540 million property tax base, the limit drops to ₩10 million.

items.q: Is the property tax base different from the published price?
items.a: Yes. The property tax base for land, buildings and houses is the standard value (published price) multiplied by the fair market value ratio, so it is lower than the published price (Local Tax Act Art. 110). The dependent test uses the sum for land, buildings, houses, ships and aircraft; rental deposits are not included. Your tax base is on your property tax bill.

items.q: When can status be lost, and which year's income counts?
items.a: From November, the review uses the previous year's income and that year's June 1 property data. From January to October, income from two years before is used (pensions: the previous year) (Decree Art. 41(3), NHIS Articles Art. 43-4). If the requirements are not met, status ends the day after the NHIS confirms it (Rule Art. 2(3)).

items.q: Can a sibling be a dependent?
items.a: Only siblings under 30, 65 or older, registered disabled, or merit/veteran recipients with a disability grade. They must be never married (divorced or widowed counts), and the specified family members, such as parents, must have no wages or income. The property limit is stricter at a ₩180 million tax base (Rule Annexes 1 and 1-2).

items.q: Is financial income of ₩10 million or less excluded for dependents?
items.a: For premium calculations, interest and dividends totalling ₩10 million or less are not added (Rule Art. 44(1) proviso). Whether the dependent income test uses the same rule is not clearly confirmed in the rules or NHIS guidance. This calculator includes financial income and tells you when excluding it would change the result. Please confirm with the NHIS (1577-1000).

items.q: If income drops after closing a business, can they become a dependent again?
items.a: If income falls for reasons set by the NHIS, such as closing a business, you can submit proof and apply for an income adjustment (Decree Art. 41-2). According to the NHIS, reporting the dependent within 90 days of the adjustment application makes it effective from the application date.
